corrections.source_says: The main study is a counterbalanced within-person comparison of two AI configurations; randomized order is not stated. Use design_class="other" with that description, retain assignment.randomized="not_stated" and criterion_1="unclear", and remove the claim that this is a randomized-type experiment. context_class="none" can remain provisional: an unstated allocation method does not establish either an RCT or a definitively non-random observational design. No randomized AI-assistance study is documented in this version.
corrections.quote: The order of system use (i.e., which system was used first) was counterbalanced across participants to mitigate order effects.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 12, Sections 5.2.4 and 5.3.2; formative-study sampling is described separately on p. 4, Section 3.1.1; creativity-codebook.md Sections 3-4.

corrections.source_says: Add expert-rated Complexity and Completeness from Table 10. Complexity is Reflexa 3.56 (SD 1.41) versus baseline 2.19 (SD 1.34), t = 4.31, p < .001; Completeness is 3.83 (SD 1.36) versus 3.38 (SD 1.29), t = 5.68, p < .001, exactly as printed. Expert-rated Evolution is also reported in Table 12: Reflexa mean v1 to v4 is 3.35 to 4.54 (Friedman p = 0.001, Page p < .001), and baseline is 3.20 to 4.22 (Friedman p = 0.012, Page p < .001). Those are separate within-system trend tests, not tests of a between-system Evolution contrast; Table 10 supplies no expert Evolution mean/SD contrast. Mention the version-wise results for the other expert outcomes as supplementary analyses.

corrections.source_says: Use not_stated for preregistration and primary-outcome status, because neither is identified. The sketches were produced during the AI-assisted sessions, so AI availability is yes and output timing is immediate. Describe the expert ratings and averaging across successive versions in measure_detail. All three listed contrasts have direction=treatment_higher, and Table 10 reports arm means/SDs and t statistics with p-values; statistics_available should at least include test_statistic rather than remain empty. The table gives no test-specific n or degrees of freedom, so do not infer additional people or independent rating counts from it.

confirmed: Read the complete 154078-character markdown, including references and Appendices A-C; checked relevant PDF text and Table 10 column alignment independently. The PDF has 30 pages and identifies arXiv:2601.17769v1 [cs.HC], 25 Jan 2026 (PDF p. 1).

The document title and authors match the form: Anqi Wang, Zhengyi Li, Lan Luo, Xin Tong and Pan Hui (PDF p. 1). The ACM dates/DOI placeholders do not establish a journal or conference version of record.

The comparative user study recruited 18 artists and analyzes the same people across both systems; n_analyzed=18 overall and 18 in each repeated condition does not mean separate groups. The methods explicitly identify the analysis sample as N=18, and Table 5 lists P1-P18 (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 13, Section 5.4; p. 28, Table 5).

No number randomized or participant exclusions is reported for the comparative study, so the null randomized counts are appropriate. Fewer than 50 people were analyzed, and core=no and criterion_2=not_met are correct (PDF pp. 11-13, Sections 5.1-5.4).

The artists have prior Processing/p5.js and LLM experience, were recruited purposively, and received $14 USD for approximately 120 minutes; Table 5 gives ages from 19 to 31 and artistic professions (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 28, Table 5).

Each participant used both systems for a 30-minute session, producing four exploratory sketch versions per system and eight per person. The p5.js task required at least one interactive element and at least two adjustable parameters; sketches and versions are outputs, not extra participants (PDF p. 12, Sections 5.2.4 and 5.3.2).

Both conditions provide generative-AI code assistance, and the comparison concerns reflection scaffolds added to the same LLM/editor/preview. The task and comparison descriptions design_visual, with_ai and ai_design are supported (PDF p. 11, Sections 4.2.3 and 5; p. 12, Sections 5.2.3 and 5.3.2).

Three expert evaluators rated the creative outputs on the same 7-point scale used for participant assessments. Methods state that scores were averaged across four successive versions and systems compared using paired t-tests or Wilcoxon tests; these expert output ratings support criterion_3=met (PDF p. 13, Sections 5.3.3-5.4).
S1-O1 reported string matches: expert Originality, Reflexa 3.67 (SD 1.56), baseline 3.27 (SD 1.40), t=5.51, p<.001 (PDF p. 29, Table 10, Expert-Evaluated columns).
S1-O2 reported string matches: expert Novelty, Reflexa 3.67 (SD 1.54), baseline 3.33 (SD 1.33), t=3.39, p=0.001 (PDF p. 29, Table 10, Expert-Evaluated columns).
S1-O3 reported string matches: expert Aesthetic, Reflexa 4.10 (SD 1.60), baseline 3.60 (SD 1.44), t=4.59, p<.001 (PDF p. 29, Table 10, Expert-Evaluated columns).
The one-line finding accurately reports the 18-person within-subjects comparison and all three expert-rated between-system results (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 12, Section 5.2.4; p. 29, Table 10).

This is an empirical system-design/user-study paper, not a synthesis; no pooled estimate, synthesis study count or meta-analytic standardizer is reported, so the synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF pp. 4-7, Section 3; pp. 11-19, Sections 5-8).

No confirmed randomized people study was found: the main study only specifies counterbalancing, and the formative workshop randomizes sampling/group organization without an AI-treatment comparison (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1.1; p. 12, Sections 5.2.4 and 5.3.2). The false flag means random assignment is unconfirmed in this version, not that the authors explicitly ruled it out.
summary: The arXiv v1 reports an 18-person counterbalanced comparison, but no randomized assignment to AI assistance is documented. The recorded Table 10 statistics and one-line finding are accurate; corrections concern the RCT label, omitted studies/outcomes and metadata, the baseline embedding-model claim, and appendix/section locators.
